brief.summary: A free spaced-repetition flashcard app used by millions of students and hobby learners that also lets anyone dig into their own study history to see what they remember and forget.
brief.user: Mariana Duque, a 16-year-old high-school junior who has used the app for a year for AP Spanish and AP Biology. She knows nothing about statistics. She opened the insights area out of curiosity because she feels like she's "getting worse".
brief.moment: Her success rate on Biology reviews dropped from about 88% to 71% over the past three weeks, and she wants to know why before her unit test on cell respiration next Friday. Her guesses: she's been studying late at night, she added too many new cards at once, or the new cards are just harder. She wants to compare her recall across decks, times of day and card age, notice which explanation the data actually supports, and click into the specific cards she keeps missing.
brief.data: She has 2,140 cards across 5 decks: AP Bio Unit 3 (412 cards, 186 added in the last 3 weeks), AP Bio Units 1–2 (530), Spanish Vocab (860), Spanish Verb Conjugations (240) and Periodic Table (98). Her history covers 9,800 reviews over the last 42 days. Each review has a timestamp, the answer she gave (again/hard/good/easy), response time in seconds, and the card's age and interval. Reviews after 10:30pm make up 38% of recent sessions. Her streak is 61 days. The 25 cards she misses most are mostly Krebs cycle and electron transport chain cards; one card ("Net ATP from glycolysis") was failed 9 times.

prompt:
I need the front end for Recallery. A free spaced-repetition flashcard app used by millions of students and hobby learners that also lets anyone dig into their own study history to see what they remember and forget.

Who's using it: Mariana Duque, a 16-year-old high-school junior who has used the app for a year for AP Spanish and AP Biology. She knows nothing about statistics. She opened the insights area out of curiosity because she feels like she's "getting worse".

What they're doing right now: Her success rate on Biology reviews dropped from about 88% to 71% over the past three weeks, and she wants to know why before her unit test on cell respiration next Friday. Her guesses: she's been studying late at night, she added too many new cards at once, or the new cards are just harder. She wants to compare her recall across decks, times of day and card age, notice which explanation the data actually supports, and click into the specific cards she keeps missing.

What's in the system at this point: She has 2,140 cards across 5 decks: AP Bio Unit 3 (412 cards, 186 added in the last 3 weeks), AP Bio Units 1–2 (530), Spanish Vocab (860), Spanish Verb Conjugations (240) and Periodic Table (98). Her history covers 9,800 reviews over the last 42 days. Each review has a timestamp, the answer she gave (again/hard/good/easy), response time in seconds, and the card's age and interval. Reviews after 10:30pm make up 38% of recent sessions. Her streak is 61 days. The 25 cards she misses most are mostly Krebs cycle and electron transport chain cards; one card ("Net ATP from glycolysis") was failed 9 times.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
